title: Basic English — Course 2, Semester 1 — Pilot Variant 14

tasks.prompt: Listening 1. When do the presentation skills lessons take place?
tasks.audioText: The college is offering students a choice of two optional short courses next term. The first course focuses on presentation skills and meets on Mondays. The second introduces basic project management and meets on Wednesdays. Both courses have the same number of lessons. Students should read the descriptions and submit their preference by the end of the month.

tasks.prompt: Listening 2. When should students submit their preference?
tasks.audioText: The college is offering students a choice of two optional short courses next term. The first course focuses on presentation skills and meets on Mondays. The second introduces basic project management and meets on Wednesdays. Both courses have the same number of lessons. Students should read the descriptions and submit their preference by the end of the month.
options: By the end of the month

tasks.prompt: Maksim wanted to improve his communication skills, but he was also interested in learning how to organise projects. He compared the course descriptions and checked his timetable. The project management course fitted his schedule better, while presentation skills were already included in another college activity. He chose project management and saved the course confirmation. Reading 1. Which course did Maksim choose?
Why did he make that choice?
options: It fitted his schedule and presentation skills were covered elsewhere

tasks.prompt: This course is ___ than the one I attended last term.
Choose TWO factors to consider when selecting an optional course.
options: The colour of the course website
Whether it supports your learning goals

tasks.prompt: A decision made after comparing possibilities is a ___.
You need more information before choosing a course. What should you ask?
options: Could you explain what topics the course covers?

tasks.prompt: Put the stages of making decisions in a sensible order.
options: Identify what you want to learn
correctOrder: Identify what you want to learn

tasks.prompt: Write 60–80 words comparing two optional courses. Explain which one you would choose and give two reasons.
tasks.rubric: 8 points total: two optional courses are identified and a relevant difference is explained (0–2); one course is selected and supported by two clear reasons (0–2); comparative forms and basic grammar are understandable (0–2); course/education vocabulary, spelling and punctuation are appropriate (0–2).
